svg.title: How scheduled_jobs is built, used and rebuilt
svg.desc: Plan() routes each pending job either into plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs (planned) or straight into result.scheduled_jobs (failed); at the end the planned ones are labelled, rebuilt and appended to result.

g.text: for each entry of plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs: job.state = STATE_EXECUTING; RETRIEVE: bay_id, bay_arrival_node_guid; result.scheduled_jobs.push_back(entry)

g.text: Event counts and the rebuild order are illustrative. If a later stage (tray or AGV assignment, CHUGG) fails, Plan() instead returns early and appends a FailJob entry for every pending job.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: How scheduled_jobs is built, used and rebuilt

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Each pending job goes to exactly one list during the loop: plan_ctx->scheduled_jobs if its job method succeeds, result.scheduled_jobs (as a FailJob entry) if it fails. Planned jobs reach result only at the very end.
